meta.title: Frely CLI — Your AI. On your terms.
meta.description: Frely CLI connects remote MCP clients to local tools and shares local models through Frely. Open source. Install with npm or download a standalone executable.

tools.label: LOCAL TOOLS / MCP
tools.description: Connect a remote MCP client to local files, shell commands, and persistent processes. Approve your device and workspace in the browser, then add the stable MCP URL to your client.
tools.note: Local execution requires your approval. Shell commands run with your OS user’s permissions; the workspace is not a shell sandbox.
agents.label: REMOTE AGENTS / IN DEVELOPMENT
agents.description: Remote Agent integration is under development. It is not included in the npm release verified for this page, 0.6.1.
agents.note: The planned flow invokes a hosted Frely Agent without changing your host’s model provider. Installation instructions will follow a verified supporting release.
models.label: LOCAL MODELS / PROVIDERS
models.description: Connect a running Ollama or another loopback OpenAI-compatible runtime as a personal Frely Provider. Use it through your existing Frely Access Points and API keys.
models.note: Requires a running local model and an empty, active personal Provider slot. Sharing a Provider does not enable local MCP execution.
install.description: Install the CLI, sign in, then choose your workflow.
install.node: The npm package requires Node.js 22 or newer.
source.description: Frely CLI and this page are open source. Explore the code, report an issue, or contribute your next improvement.
source.note: The CLI connects to Frely’s hosted Relay service. The open-source client and local MCP runtime are licensed under Apache-2.0; Frely trademarks remain reserved.
footer.note: A little closer to your machine.
copy.failure: Copy unavailable. The command is selected; use your device’s copy action.
tools.prepare: Run these commands inside the folder you intend to share. Complete the device and workspace approval in your browser, and keep this computer running and online.
tools.connect: Add the exact URL printed by frely mcp url to a remote MCP client that supports OAuth. Select OAuth and complete the client’s authorization flow.
tools.verify: In that client, ask Frely to list the top-level names in your selected workspace without writing files or running shell commands. The connection is verified when the tool returns names you can match to that folder.
tools.diagnostics: If the call fails, run frely doctor --mcp and frely mcp service status. A diagnostic pass alone does not verify the client’s OAuth connection or a completed tool call.
models.verify: Next, use this Provider through a Frely Access Point and make a request with its API key. Verify a real response from the selected model; a Provider list entry alone does not prove inference works.
install.diagnostics: This checks the CLI and account setup. Unconfigured MCP is optional here; passing does not mean a remote client is connected.
install.next: Choose a workflow and follow it through to a real tool result or model response.
